title: Mirror & Water Images
summary: A vertical mirror reverses left-right (character order reversed and every character flipped); water reverses top-bottom (order kept, characters upside down). Know the symmetric letters for each (AHIMOTUVWXY for mirrors, BCDEHIKOX for water), use 11:60 − time for clock mirrors, and track one asymmetric feature in figure questions.

subtopics.title: Mirror images (vertical mirror)
subtopics.concept:
A mirror placed **vertically** (to the left or right of the object — the result is the same) swaps **left and right** but keeps **top and bottom**. For a word or number this does two things at once:

1. the **order** of characters is reversed (the last character appears first), and
2. **each character is flipped** left-to-right (R faces the other way, 4 turns round).

Letters with a vertical axis of symmetry — **A H I M O T U V W X Y** — look unchanged when flipped, so they are the fastest check points; asymmetric ones like **B C D E F G J K L N P Q R S Z** and digits **2 3 4 5 6 7 9** decide between options.

tricks.title: Check the end characters first
tricks.body: In a vertical-mirror image the last character of the original stands first, flipped. Eliminate options by looking only at the first and last characters.

example.q:
**Q.** Mirror image of PEN7?

**Sol.** The image starts with a flipped 7 and ends with a flipped P. Any option starting with a normal P (order not reversed) or a normal 7 (not flipped) is wrong.
example.solution: Reversed order + flipped characters — test both on one end.

tricks.title: Symmetric-letter shortcut
tricks.body: A word made only of A H I M O T U V W X Y that reads the same backwards (a palindrome, e.g. TOOT, WOW) looks identical in a vertical mirror.

example.q:
**Q.** Does MOM look the same in a vertical mirror?

**Sol.** M, O are symmetric and MOM is a palindrome → yes.

mistakes: Flipping each letter but keeping the original order.
Reversing the order but not flipping the asymmetric letters.
Confusing the mirror image with the water image (top-bottom flip).

subtopics.title: Water images (horizontal mirror)
subtopics.concept:
A water surface acts as a **horizontal** mirror below the object: it swaps **top and bottom** and keeps **left and right**. So in a water image:

- the **order** of characters stays the same, and
- each character is turned **upside down** (flipped top-to-bottom, not rotated).

Letters with a horizontal axis of symmetry — **B C D E H I K O X** (and digits 0, 3, 8) — look unchanged in water. A word made only of these letters (CHOICE, CODE, HIDE, BOX) looks identical in water.

A mirror image followed by a water image is the same as a **half-turn (180° rotation)**.

tricks.title: Order stays, letters go upside down
tricks.body: Scan the options for the one that keeps the original order and has only asymmetric letters turned upside down.

example.q:
**Q.** Water image of BOX?

**Sol.** B, O, X are all top-bottom symmetric, and water keeps the order → BOX looks unchanged.
example.solution: Water image: same order, top-bottom flip.

mistakes: Reversing the character order in a water image.
Rotating letters by 180° instead of flipping them top-to-bottom.

subtopics.title: Mirror image of a clock
subtopics.concept:
When a clock is seen in a vertical mirror, both hands swap sides of the 12–6 line. The time shown by the image and the actual time always **add up to 12:00** (on a 12-hour clock).

So: **image time = 11:60 − actual time** (and actual = 11:60 − image, the same rule both ways). Writing 12:00 as 11:60 avoids borrowing.

Exception: if the actual time is 12:00 or 6:00, the image shows the same time. For times between 12:00 and 1:00 (like 12:20), use 23:60 − time (answer 11:40).

Water images of clocks usually put the hour hand in a position that no real time matches, so exams mostly ask about mirror images.

formulas.name: Mirror time
formulas.note: Works in both directions; for 12:xx use 23:60 − T.

tricks.title: 11:60 rule
tricks.body: Subtract the time from 11:60 digit-group-wise: hours from 11, minutes from 60.

example.q:
**Q.** A clock shows 4:20. What does its mirror image show?

**Sol.** 11:60 − 4:20 = **7:40**.

mistakes: Subtracting from 12:00 and mis-borrowing the minutes.
Applying the rule to 12:xx without adding 12 first.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A word, code or number with four image options.
pyqPatterns.approach: Reversed order + each letter flipped; check first and last characters.
Order unchanged; asymmetric letters upside down.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Time seen in a mirror, or actual time from a mirror reading.
How many letters of a word look the same in a mirror / in water.
pyqPatterns.approach: Match against A H I M O T U V W X Y (mirror) or B C D E H I K O X (water).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A line figure with four image options.
pyqPatterns.approach: Track one asymmetric feature (a flag, a notch) to its reflected position.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Which word looks exactly the same in the mirror / in water.
pyqPatterns.approach: Mirror: symmetric letters + palindrome. Water: all letters top-bottom symmetric.

solvedExamples.solution: A vertical mirror reverses the order and flips every letter left-to-right. So the image reads K N A L P from left to right, with K, N, L, P facing the other way (A is symmetric and looks the same). The option with reversed order **and** flipped letters is correct; the others show the water image, only a reversed order, or only flipped letters.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Look at the first character: it must be a flipped K.

solvedExamples.q: How many letters of the word **MATHEMATICS** look exactly the same in a vertical mirror (considered one by one)?
solvedExamples.solution: Left-right symmetric capitals: A H I M O T U V W X Y. In M A T H E M A T I C S, the symmetric ones are M, A, T, H, M, A, T, I = **8**; E, C, S are not.

practice.solution: Reverse the order (5 2 M A X E) and flip each character left-to-right. M, A, X are symmetric; 5, 2 and E face the other way. Only one option has both features.
practice.shortcut: The image starts with a flipped 5.

practice.q: A wall clock shows **3:45**. What time will its mirror image show?
A wall clock shows **10:10**. What time will its mirror image show?
A wall clock shows **6:35**. What time will its mirror image show?
Seen in a mirror, a clock appears to show **2:25**. What is the actual time?
practice.solution: The rule works both ways: actual = 11:60 − 2:25 = **9:35**. Check: mirror of 9:35 = 11:60 − 9:35 = 2:25.

practice.q: A clock shows **12:20**. What time does its mirror image show?
practice.solution: For 12:xx times use 23:60: 23:60 − 12:20 = 11:40. Check: 12:20 + 11:40 = 24:00, i.e. the hands mirror across the 12–6 line → **11:40**.

practice.q: Which of the following words will look **exactly the same** in a vertical mirror?
options: DEED
BOB
WOW
NOON
practice.solution: A word looks unchanged in a vertical mirror only if (i) it reads the same backwards and (ii) every letter is left-right symmetric (A H I M O T U V W X Y). All four are palindromes, but N, D and B are not left-right symmetric. Only **WOW** passes both tests.

practice.q: Which of the following words will look **exactly the same** in its water image?
options: BRIDGE
CHANCE
EXPECT
CHOICE
practice.solution: Water keeps the order, so a word is unchanged only if every letter is top-bottom symmetric (B C D E H I K O X). CHOICE = C, H, O, I, C, E — all symmetric. BRIDGE has R and G, CHANCE has A and N, EXPECT has P and T. Answer: **CHOICE**.
practice.shortcut: Every letter must be in BCDEHIKOX.

practice.q: How many letters of the word **BACKGROUND** look exactly the same in a water image (considered one by one)?
practice.solution: Top-bottom symmetric capitals: B C D E H I K O X. Letter by letter in B A C K G R O U N D: B ✓, A ✗, C ✓, K ✓, G ✗, R ✗, O ✓, U ✗, N ✗, D ✓ → **5**.

practice.solution: A vertical mirror swaps left and right only. The flag, which points to the right of the pole, will point to the **left** in the image, and it stays at the **top**; the foot line (which extends to the right of the pole) moves to the left side. The option showing a left-pointing flag at the top is correct — a flag at the bottom is the water image, and a flag at the bottom pointing left is the half-turn.

practice.solution: A water image swaps top and bottom only. The boot's toe (the wide part) is at the bottom-right in the figure; in water it moves to the **top-right**, and the shaft with its strap line now hangs downward on the left. Left and right do not change, so the toe must still be on the right. The option with the toe at the top-right is correct.
